patents.source: USPTO Open Data Portal, granted patents since 2001, applicant phrase "leidos", 2026-10-05

reading.body:
Leidos holds 114 granted patents and no recorded AI products, which places it in the defense and infrastructure services business rather than the model business.

The patent record is broad rather than concentrated. Recent grants cover synthetic data generation with masked transformers, a robotic divestiture system, visual feedback, mobile ad hoc network time synchronization, and a PD-1 and CTLA-4 dual inhibitor peptide. That spread matches a contractor that builds to government and health requirements across several domains instead of pushing one platform.

For AI scaling, the relevant fact is what is absent. There is no data center, power, or compute footprint here, and no AI product line. Leidos appears as a services and mission software supplier, which means it sits downstream of compute rather than constraining it. The NorthStar 2030 growth engines named in its own description, space and maritime, energy infrastructure, digital modernization and cyber, mission software, and managed health, are where its work is aimed.

The limits are worth stating plainly. The patent count comes from a single applicant phrase search of granted patents since 2001, so it undercounts anything filed under a different name and says nothing about pending applications. The filing list covers eight SEC submissions between March and October 2026 and does not include their contents. Nothing here establishes revenue, contract value, or how much of this work touches AI at all.

profile_text.body:
Leidos is a publicly traded company, listed under the ticker LDOS, that describes itself as a Fortune 500 digital and mission innovator delivering solutions at the intersection of national security, health, and critical infrastructure. According to its website, it has a global workforce of approximately 47,000 and is carrying out a strategy it calls NorthStar 2030, focused on five growth engines: space and maritime, energy infrastructure, digital modernization and cyber, mission software, and managed health. The site also notes recruiting in North Alabama, which it describes as a center for defense, aerospace, and manufacturing.

The harvested material does not describe specific AI products or services, and no products are tracked for the company. Its stated areas of work include digital modernization and cyber and mission software, but the site text does not detail AI offerings.

The company's record lists no lawsuits and no MCP servers. It is registered with the SEC under CIK 0001336920.
